purpose: This is the normative authorization policy for the shipped Courtside API. OpenAPI defines the transport shape; this policy defines who may perform each operation, which resource attributes narrow that permission, and which protected fields each projection may read or write.

operationRules.description: Build metadata, the API document, login status and idempotent logout are available without permanent account authority.
Login accepts credentials from an anonymous or existing browser only through the dedicated form fields and never returns them.
Public club configuration, facilities and calendar occupancy are readable without account authority through deliberately bounded response projections.
An account carrying an issued credential may replace it but may perform no ordinary authenticated operation first.
Permanent accounts may read their sessions and change only the locale and message choices attached to their own account.
A permanent account may prove or replace only its own password through the dedicated credential operations.
A permanent account may terminate its own sessions; ending every session or another browser additionally requires a recent password proof.
Permanent accounts may discover active booking cards admitted by their roles for future booking requests.
Permanent accounts may discover the active participant-card types available when naming a booking participant.
Permanent accounts may search the bounded current-member projection used to name a participant in their own booking request.
A permanent account may create or preview bookings only with a booking card admitted by its roles and the current resource state.
A permanent account sees its own bookings and participations and may mutate only an owned booking or its own participation; administrators retain the documented booking override.
A permanent account sees booking management data only when one of its roles manages the booking card; administrators may manage every card.
Series cancellation and movement require ownership of the series or a booking-card management role; administrators retain the documented override.
Ordinary administration requires an enabled permanent account carrying ADMIN; operation-specific validation and state guards still apply.
Correcting a person's identity or address requires ADMIN and a recent full-password proof.
Creating or correcting account security and terminating one account's sessions requires ADMIN and a recent full-password proof.
Changing roles or enabled state requires ADMIN, recent authentication and preservation of at least one enabled administrator.
Terminating every account session requires ADMIN and recent authentication and also ends the caller's current session.
Executing a reviewed import requires ADMIN, recent authentication and ownership of a current preview whose source and roster state still match.

decisions.title: Public request boundary
decisions.rule: Only explicitly public routes admit an anonymous caller; all other shipped operations require a valid server-side session.

decisions.title: Permanent account gate
decisions.rule: Ordinary account operations require an authenticated, enabled account whose issued credential has already been replaced by a permanent password.

decisions.title: Initial password gate
decisions.rule: The initial-password authority reaches only password replacement and loses all authority when that replacement succeeds.

decisions.title: Administrator gate
decisions.rule: Every route below /api/admin requires ADMIN and rejects anonymous, initial-password and every non-admin product role before the operation runs.

decisions.title: Own account scope
decisions.rule: The authenticated account identifier selects session, locale and message-choice state; callers cannot supply another account identifier to these operations.

decisions.title: Credential write-only boundary
decisions.rule: Passwords are accepted only by their dedicated credential workflows, never returned in a response and never accepted by account administration.

decisions.title: Booking card role and state
decisions.rule: A booking card must be active and admit at least one actor role; ADMIN bypasses the card role list but not facility availability or invariant checks.

decisions.title: Booking and participation ownership
decisions.rule: Personal queries derive identity from the current account; cancellation requires the booking owner or ADMIN and withdrawal removes only the current person's participation.

decisions.title: Participant card availability
decisions.rule: Participant-card discovery returns active cards only; it has no booking-card role allowlist or administrator override.

decisions.title: Managed booking scope
decisions.rule: Managed listings and details contain only bookings whose card names one of the actor roles as a managing role; ADMIN sees every card.

decisions.title: Series ownership and management
decisions.rule: Moving or cancelling a series requires its creator, a role that manages the series booking card, or ADMIN; the selected occurrence scope is preserved.

decisions.title: Recent full-password proof
decisions.rule: Sensitive account administration, another browser's session termination and import execution require a successful full-password proof no older than five minutes.

decisions.title: Administrator continuity
decisions.rule: The last enabled administrator cannot remove its ADMIN role or disable its account; another enabled administrator makes the same transition permissible.

decisions.title: Import preview ownership and state
decisions.rule: Only the administrator who created a current, unexpired preview may execute it, and execution rechecks its source and roster fingerprints before any write.

decisions.title: Import preview read projection
decisions.rule: Every administrator may read a stored preview; after its retention expires, personal change details and ignored columns are removed while non-personal counts and hashes remain.

decisions.title: Public response projection
decisions.rule: Public configuration and calendar responses use dedicated DTO projections and never widen to administrative configuration, roster or another person's booking details.

decisions.title: Participant directory projection
decisions.rule: Participant search returns only the stable person identifier and display name of current members, never roster, account, address or membership administration fields.

decisions.title: Administrative response projection
decisions.rule: Administrative DTOs may expose the documented roster and operational fields to ADMIN only; credentials remain absent and subject access omits other people's booking data.

fieldRules.description: A username and password are accepted only by form login and never occur in an API response.
Session identity fields describe only the account attached to the current session and become absent or empty for an anonymous caller.
Opaque revocation handles and normalized browser metadata are visible only to the account that owns those sessions.
The issued credential replacement is accepted only by the initial-password operation and is never part of a response projection.
The current and replacement passwords are accepted only by the own-password operation and never appear in a response projection.
A password proof is accepted only by the reauthentication operation and never appears in a response projection.
Current member lookup exposes only the identifier and display name needed to add that member to a booking.
The public allocation projection withholds booker identity; participant surnames appear only on the authenticated viewer's own booking.
A booking note and personal booking identifiers are returned only through the current account's own booking projection.
Participant display names and internal notes appear only in the detail of a booking whose card the actor may manage.
Names and email addresses can be introduced only through the dedicated administrative person creation workflow.
Correcting a person's names or email address requires both administrator authority and recent full-password proof.
An account identifier and its initial roles are writable only through account creation after a recent administrator password proof.
An account username is replaceable only through its dedicated operation after a recent administrator password proof.
Replacing account roles requires recent administrator proof and preserves at least one enabled administrator in the instance.
Replacing account enabled state requires recent administrator proof and preserves at least one enabled administrator in the instance.
Full person, membership and account state is confined to administrative roster responses and never contains a password or reusable session credential.
Credential lifetimes and the no-membership rule assignment are visible only in the administrative configuration projection.
Credential lifetimes, reminder timing and the no-membership rule assignment can be changed only through the administrator configuration operation.
A participant's person identifier or guest name is accepted only as part of the current account's authorized individual booking request.
A recurring booking note is accepted only as part of the current account's authorized series preview or creation request.
Audit actor data, parameters and resolved subject names are available only to administrators through the audit log.
Message identifiers and recipient metadata are available only to administrators through the message log.
The subject-access projection is administrator-only and contains data about exactly the selected person while excluding other people's booking notes and identities.
External member identifiers and their person links are confined to dedicated administrator reference operations.
Previewed person values and possible matches are visible to administrators until the preview retention expires and the personal change set is removed.
